resources.string: Hold the button below and speak.\n\nYour words are turned into text on this phone, and only the text is sent to the other phone. The other phone then reads it out loud. Nothing is recorded and nothing is uploaded.
Not connected — tap Devices to link up
What we have not tested yet

Two phones, no internet needed.

You hold the button and speak. This phone works out what you said and turns it into written words. It then sends just those words to the other phone, which reads them out loud.

Your actual voice is never sent and never recorded. Only the written words travel — and written words are around 480 times smaller than speech, which is the whole point: a weak or damaged radio link can carry a sentence even when it could never carry a voice.
All ten required languages are understood. Six of them are also spoken aloud by this app; the other four show the words on screen but stay silent, and the app tells you so rather than pretending.

We tested speech recognition on 2,000 real recordings of real people speaking — about 6 hours and 40 minutes of audio, the same set for every language.

On average, 9 out of every 100 letters came out wrong. That sounds alarming, but a mistake is usually one letter inside an otherwise correct word.

English and Hindi are the most accurate. Tamil and Odia are the weakest — roughly 1 word in 2 contains a mistake. If you try those, expect errors.

We would rather list these than have you find them.

• Two phones have never actually been tested against each other. The Bluetooth connection has never completed a real conversation. This is the most important thing still to prove.

• No human has listened to the voices yet and judged them. Every “how clear is the speech” number we have comes from a computer feeding the audio back into itself, which is not the same as a person understanding it in a stressful situation.

• We tested with recorded background noise added afterwards. We have not recorded anyone speaking in a real disaster.
This was built for a problem statement set by ISRO, Department of Space.
A two-way radio that works on a bad connection, using 10 Indian languages

iTantra is mostly not our code. The speech recognition, the voices, the speech engine and the screen design all come from other people who made their work free to use, and we are grateful for it.

This page lists every part, says in plain words what it does, and points you at the original so you can check us.

Two of them carry conditions you should know about, and they are marked clearly below.
